size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z, const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Compute Laplacian with clamped boundary const size_t xn = (x > 0) ? x - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t yn = (y > 0) ? y - 1 : 0;\n    const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n    \n    const double cxx = (c[idx3(xp, y, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(xn, y, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny)]) / (dx * dx);\n    const double cyy = (c[idx3(x, yp, z, nx, ny)] + c[idx3(x, yn, z, nx, ny)] - \n                  2.0 * c[idx3(x, y, ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n                c[idx] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n    \n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n    \n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n    \n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n    \n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n    \n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n    \n    size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n    \n    // Allocate arrays\n    std::vector<double> cold(gridSize);\n    std::vector<double> cnew(gridSize);\n    std::vector<double> mu(gridSize);\n    \n    // Initialize concentration  auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    \n    for (int t = 0; t < iterations; ++t) {\n        // Compute chemical potential\n        computeChemicalPotential(cold, mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, \n                                gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB);\n        \n        // Update concentration\n        cahnHilliardUpdate(cnew, cold, mu, nx, ny, nz, D, dt, dx, dy, dz);\n const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n                                         const double D, const double dt,\n                                         const double dx, const double ny, x, y, z);\n\n    cnew[linear] = cold[linear] + dt * D * computeLaplacian(mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, x, y, z);\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t maxVal = std::max(maxVal, val);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n\n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0         printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n\n    const size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n\n    // Device buffers (kept resident on the GPU for the whole run)\n    double *d_cold = nullptr, *d_cnew = nullptr, *d_mu = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cold, gridSize * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cnew, gridSize * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_mu, gridSize * sizeof(double)));\n\n    const unsigned int numBlocks = static_cast<unsigned int>((gridSize + BLOCK_SIZE - 1) / BLOCK_SIZE);\n\n    // Initialize concentration field on the GPU\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n    if (gridSize > 0) {\n        initializeConcentrationKernel<<<numBlocks, BLOCK_SIZE>>>(d_cold, nx, ny, nz);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n    // Run simulation\n    printf(\"Running Cahn-Hilliard simulation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    for (int t = 0; t < iterations && gridSize > 0; ++t) {\n        // Compute At 16.7M cells, each step takes roughly 5ms, and I'm estimating the memory traffic involved in reading concentration and writing chemical potential per step.\n\nWorking through the ideal bandwidth comparison against the actual 5ms runtime shows I'm about 7x off ideal, likely due to stencil reads crossing cache lines for neighboring rows and planes. I'm sketching a tiled kernel design for the Laplacian using 32x8 thread blocks with a sliding window across z-planes, weighing whether to load halos into shared memory versus relying on cached global reads for z-neighbors, and considering whether fusing the mu and update kernels is feasible given the neighbor dependency.\n\nI need to make sure clamped boundary handling stays bit-identical to the original version by loading clamped global indices into the shared tile rather than changing the math itself.\n\nWriting the tiled kernel template...\n\nI'm keeping the update expression as `cold + dt*D*lap` with left-to-right multiplication order, and preserving the laplacian division by dx*dx exactly as original since dx=1.0 anyway. For the tile design, I'm planning a 32x8 thread block with a shared memory tile sized 34x10 doubles (~2720 bytes), looping each thread over the z-dimension.\n\nReconsidering that per-thread z-marching approach though—it only gives 64 blocks for a 256^2 grid, which is way too few for good occupancy across 82 SMs. Switching to a full 3D tiling scheme instead: each block covers a 32x8x1 slice at a fixed z, giving 65536 total blocks (8*32*256), with z-neighbor values pulled from global memory (likely cached in L2) and a modest 1.33x halo overhead for the shared tile loads—this should scale much better.\n\nI'm also running into CUDA's grid dimension limits: gridDim.y and gridDim.z are both capped at 65535, so for large nz or ny I need grid-stride loops inside the kernel to iterate over tiles beyond that cap, rather than relying on a 1:1 block-to-tile mapping. Writing the tiling and stride-loop logic...\n\nStill writing kernel loop structure...\n\nStill writing halo-loading logic...\n\nI double-check the boundary clamping logic for edge cases at x=0 and x=nx-1, confirming the halo values correctly fall back to the center value rather than going out of bounds, and the shared memory layout avoids bank conflicts. Then I move on to computing the Laplacian using the neighboring tile values.\n\nNow I'm designing the operator functors: one for the chemical potential combining the cubic nonlinearity with the gradient energy term, and another for the time-stepping update that applies diffusion using the Laplacian of the potential.\n\nI need to make sure tile loading in shared memory is properly synchronized — adding a syncthreads barrier after each tile iteration before the next load overwrites it, and confirming threads outside the domain still participate safely in loads. I'm also dropping the now-unnecessary decode function while keeping the 1D init kernel and the idx3 indexing helper.\n\nFor the stencil offsets, I'll use signed long long arithmetic to safely handle negative clamped indices near domain boundaries before casting back. The grid is configured with tile-sized blocks and a 3D grid capped at CUDA's max dimension limits, skipping launches when grid size is zero, and I'm using a templated functor with a device-side operator() so different stencil operations can be passed by value into the kernel launch.\n\nRather than patching the kernel block piecemeal, it's cleaner to rewrite the whole file section covering the index computation through the update kernel, so I'll redo it as a full rewrite.\n\n","time":{"start":1793107110440,"end":1793107132742},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}

                                               \\\n        if (err_ != cudaSuccess) {                                                \\\n            fprintf(stderr, \"CUDA error at %s:%d: %s\\n\", __FILE__, __LINE__,      \\\n                    cudaGetErrorString(err_));                                    \\\n            exit(EXIT_FAILURE);                                                   \\\n        }                                                                         \\\n    } while (0)\n\n// Thread block: TILE_X threads along x (contiguous memory), TILE_Y along y.\n// Each block works on one (x, y) tile of a z-plane, staging the tile plus a\n// one-cell halo in shared memory.\nstatic constexpr int TILE_X = 32;\nstatic constexpr int TILE_Y = 8;\nstatic constexpr int THREADS_PER_BLOCK = TILE_X * TILE_Y;\nstatic constexpr unsigned int MAX_GRID_YZ = 65535;  // grid.y / grid.z hardware limit\n\n// 3D index calculation\n__host__ __device__ __forceinline__ size_t idx3(const size_t x, const size_t y, const size_t z,\n                                                const size_t nx, const size_t ny) noexcept {\n    return z * (nx * ny) + y * nx + x;\n}\n\n// Initial concentration field (pseudo-random in [-1, 1]), one thread per cell\n__global__ void initializeConcentrationKernel(double* __restrict__ c, const size_t nx, const size_t ny,\n                                              const size_t nz) {\n    const size_t vol = nx * ny * nz;\n    const size_t linear_id = static_cast<size_t>(blockIdx.x) * blockDim.x + threadIdx.x;\n    if (linear_id >= vol) return;\n\n    const double pseudo = ((((linear_id + 1) * 1299709) % vol) / static_cast<double>(vol));\n    c[linear_id] = -1.0 + 2.0 * pseudo;\n}\n\n// Chemical potential: mu = f(c) - gamma * lap(c)\nstruct ChemicalPotentialOp {\n    double gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB;\n    __device__ __forceinline__ double operator()(const double cv, const double lap, const size_t /*idx*/) const {\n        return 4.5 * ((cv + 1.0) * e_AA + (cv - 1.0) * e_BB - 2.0 * cv * e_AB)\n             + 3.0 * cv + cv * cv * cv\n             - gamma * lap;\n    }\n};\n\n// Concentration update: cnew = cold + dt * D * lap(mu)\nstruct UpdateOp {\n    const double* __restrict__ cold;\n    double D, dt;\n    __device__ __forceinline__ double operator()(const double /*muv*/, const double lap, const size_t idx) const {\n        return cold[idx] + dt * D * lap;\n    }\n};\n\n// Generic 7-point clamped-boundary stencil pass.\n// For every cell: lap = Laplacian(src)(cell), dst[cell] = op(src[cell], lap, cell).\n// The x/y neighbourhood comes from a shared-memory tile; z neighbours are read\n// from global memory. Clamped boundaries are realised by clamping the halo\n// coordinates, which yields exactly the same operands as the reference code.\ntemplate <typename Op>\n__global__ void __launch_bounds__(THREADS_PER_BLOCK)\nstencilKernel(const double* __restrict__ src, double* __restrict__ dst,\n              const size_t nx, const size_t ny, const size_t nz,\n              const double dx, const double dy, const double dz, const Op op) {\n    __shared__ double tile[TILE_Y + 2][TILE_X + 2];\n\n    const int tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const int ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const int tid = ty * TILE_X + tx;\n    const size_t tilesX = (nx + TILE_X - 1) / TILE_X;\n    const size_t tilesY = (ny + TILE_Y - 1) / TILE_Y;\n\n    // Grid-stride over tiles so that any grid size is covered.\n    for (size_t z = blockIdx.z; z < nz; z += gridDim.z) {\n        const size_t zp = (z < nz - 1) ? z + 1 : z;\n        const size_t zn = (z > 0) ? z - 1 : 0;\n\n        for (size_t by = blockIdx.y; by < tilesY; by += gridDim.y) {\n            for (size_t bx = blockIdx.x; bx < tilesX; bx += gridDim.x) {\n                const long long x0 = static_cast<long long>(bx) * TILE_X;\n                const long long y0 = static_cast<long long>(by) * TILE_Y;\n\n                // Cooperative load of the (TILE_Y+2) x (TILE_X+2) halo tile.\n                constexpr int HALO_CELLS = (TILE_Y + 2) * (TILE_X + 2);\n                for (int k = tid; k < HALO_CELLS; k += THREADS_PER_BLOCK) {\n                    const int r = k / (TILE_X + 2);\n                    const int c = k % (TILE_X + 2);\n                    long long gx = x0 + c - 1;\n                    long long gy = y0 + r - 1;\n                    gx = gx < 0 ? 0 : (gx > static_cast<long long>(nx) - 1 ? static_cast<long long>(nx) - 1 : gx);\n                    gy = gy < 0 ? 0 : (gy > static_cast<long long>(ny) - 1 ? static_cast<long long>(ny) - 1 : gy);\n                    tile[r][c] = src[idx3(static_cast<size_t>(gx), static_cast<size_t>(gy), z, nx, ny)];\n                }\n                __syncthreads();\n\n                const size_t x = static_cast<size_t>(x0) + tx;\n                const size_t y = static_cast<size_t>(y0) + ty;\n                if (x < nx && y < ny) {\n                    const double center = tile[ty + 1][tx + 1];\n                    const double xp = tile[ty + 1][tx + 2];\n                    const double xn = tile[ty + 1][tx];\n                    const double yp = tile[ty + 2][tx + 1];\n                    const double yn = tile[ty][tx + 1];\n                    const double zpv = src[idx3(x, y, zp, nx, ny)];\n                    const double znv = src[idx3(x, y, zn, nx, ny)];\n\n                    const double cxx = (xp + xn - 2.0 * center) / (dx * dx);\n                    const double cyy = (yp + yn - 2.0 * center) / (dy * dy);\n                    const double czz = (zpv + znv - 2.0 * center) / (dz * dz);\n                    const double lap = cxx + cyy + czz;\n\n                    const size_t id = idx3(x, y, z, nx, ny);\n                    dst[id] = op(center, lap, id);\n                }\n                __syncthreads();  // tile is reused by the next iteration\n            }\n        }\n    }\n}\n\nbool validateResult(const std::vector<double>& c, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nx, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t ny, [[maybe_unused]] const size_t nz) {\n    // Check for NaN or Inf\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        if (std::isnan(val) || std::isinf(val)) {\n            printf(\"Validation failed: found NaN or Inf value\\n\");\n            return false;\n        }\n    }\n\n    // Check if values are in reasonable range for concentration field\n    // After Cahn-Hilliard evolution, values should typically remain bounded\n    double minVal = c[0];\n    double maxVal = c[0];\n    for (const auto& val : c) {\n        minVal = std::min(minVal, val);\n        maxVal = std::max(maxVal, val);\n    }\n\n    printf(\"Concentration range: [%.6f, %.6f]\\n\", minVal, maxVal);\n\n    // Values should generally stay within reasonable bounds\n    if (maxVal > 10.0 || minVal < -10.0) {\n        printf(\"Validation failed: values out of expected range\\n\");\n        return false;\n    }\n\n    return true;\n}\n\nvoid printUsage(const char* progName) {\n    printf(\"Usage: %s [options]\\n\", progName);\n    printf(\"Options:\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -x <num>     Grid size in X dimension (default: 64)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -y <num>     Grid size in Y dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -z <num>     Grid size in Z dimension (default: same as X)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -i <num>     Number of time steps (default: 20)\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -v           Enable validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -r           Print results for external validation\\n\");\n    printf(\"  -h           Show this help message\\n\");\n}\n\nint main(int argc, char** argv) {\n    size_t nx = 64;\n    size_t ny = 0;\n    size_t nz = 0;\n    int iterations = 20;\n    bool validate = false;\n    bool printResults = false;\n\n    // Parse command line arguments\n    for (int i = 1; i < argc; ++i) {\n        if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-x\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nx = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-y\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            ny = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-z\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            nz = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-i\") == 0 && i + 1 < argc) {\n            iterations = atoi(argv[++i]);\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-v\") == 0) {\n            validate = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-r\") == 0) {\n            printResults = true;\n        } else if (strcmp(argv[i], \"-h\") == 0) {\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 0;\n        } else {\n            printf(\"Unknown option: %s\\n\", argv[i]);\n            printUsage(argv[0]);\n            return 1;\n        }\n    }\n\n    if (ny == 0) ny = nx;\n    if (nz == 0) nz = nx;\n\n    printf(\"Cahn-Hilliard Phase Separation Benchmark\\n\");\n    printf(\"Grid size: %zu x %zu x %zu\\n\", nx, ny, nz);\n    printf(\"Time steps: %d\\n\", iterations);\n    printf(\"Validation: %s\\n\", validate ? \"enabled\" : \"disabled\");\n\n    // Physical parameters\n    const double dx = 1.0;\n    const double dy = 1.0;\n    const double dz = 1.0;\n    const double dt = 0.01;\n    const double e_AA = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_BB = -(2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double e_AB = (2.0 / 9.0);\n    const double gamma = 0.5;\n    const double D = 1.0;\n\n    const size_t gridSize = nx * ny * nz;\n\n    // Device buffers (kept resident on the GPU for the whole run)\n    double *d_cold = nullptr, *d_cnew = nullptr, *d_mu = nullptr;\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cold, gridSize * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_cnew, gridSize * sizeof(double)));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaMalloc(&d_mu, gridSize * sizeof(double)));\n\n    // Launch configurations\n    const unsigned int initBlocks = static_cast<unsigned int>((gridSize + THREADS_PER_BLOCK - 1) / THREADS_PER_BLOCK);\n    const dim3 stencilBlock(TILE_X, TILE_Y);\n    const dim3 stencilGrid(static_cast<unsigned int>((nx + TILE_X - 1) / TILE_X),\n                           static_cast<unsigned int>(std::min<size_t>((ny + TILE_Y - 1) / TILE_Y, MAX_GRID_YZ)),\n                           static_cast<unsigned int>(std::min<size_t>(nz, MAX_GRID_YZ)));\n\n    // Initialize concentration field on the GPU\n    printf(\"Initializing concentration field...\\n\");\n    if (gridSize > 0) {\n        initializeConcentrationKernel<<<initBlocks, THREADS_PER_BLOCK>>>(d_cold, nx, ny, nz);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n    }\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n\n    // Run simulation\n    printf(\"Running Cahn-Hilliard simulation...\\n\");\n    auto start = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n\n    const ChemicalPotentialOp muOp{gamma, e_AA, e_BB, e_AB};\n    for (int t = 0; t < iterations && gridSize > 0; ++t) {\n        // Compute chemical potential: mu = f(c) - gamma * lap(c)\n        stencilKernel<<<stencilGrid, stencilBlock>>>(d_cold, d_mu, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, muOp);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n        // Update concentration: cnew = cold + dt * D * lap(mu)\n        const UpdateOp updOp{d_cold, D, dt};\n        stencilKernel<<<stencilGrid, stencilBlock>>>(d_mu, d_cnew, nx, ny, nz, dx, dy, dz, updOp);\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaGetLastError());\n\n        // Swap buffers\n        std::swap(d_cold, d_cnew);\n    }\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaDeviceSynchronize());\n    auto end = std::chrono::high_resolution_clock::now();\n    auto duration = std::chrono::duration_cast<std::chrono::milliseconds>(end - start);\n\n    printf(\"Computation time: %ld ms\\n\", duration.count());\n\n    // Calculate performance\n    double cellUpdates = (double)gridSize * iterations;\n    double mcups = cellUpdates / (duration.count() / 1000.0) / 1e6;\n    printf(\"Performance: %.3f MCellUpdates/s\\n\", mcups);\n\n    // Bring the final field back to the host only when it is needed\n    std::vector<double> cold(gridSize);\n    if ((printResults || validate) && gridSize > 0) {\n        CUDA_CHECK(cudaMemcpy(cold.data(), d_cold, gridSize * sizeof(double), cudaMemcpyDeviceToHost));\n    }\n\n    // Print results for external validation\n    if (printResults) {\n        print_results(cold, \"Concentration\");\n    }\n\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d_cold));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d_cnew));\n    CUDA_CHECK(cudaFree(d_mu));\n\n    // Validation\n {"type":"reasoning","timestamp":1793107251385,"sessionID":"ses_e827fc275ffemXp25tUfLSZTJh","part":{"id":"prt_17d853098001zpaT2aKN0EzvJi","messageID":"msg_17d852b68001G5bWqXfPAq454W","sessionID":"ses_e827fc275ffemXp25tUfLSZTJh","type":"reasoning","text":"The tiled version isn't actually faster than the flat one, so I'm questioning whether memory bandwidth is really the bottleneck. Running the math on throughput gives roughly 96 GB/s, far below the theoretical 936 GB/s peak, so something else must be limiting performance.\n\nThen it hits me: FP64 on the RTX 3090 runs at only 1/64 the rate of FP32, and I'm using three double-precision divisions per cell for dx*dx. Estimating total FP64 flops against the ~0.56 TFLOPS double-precision throughput of the 3090 gives roughly 0.36s, matching the observed runtime almost exactly — so this is clearly compute-bound on FP64 throughput, not memory bandwidth, which explains why tiling didn't help.\n\nNow I'm wondering if I can cut down the FP64 division count — since dx=1.0 is a constant, dividing by it is mathematically a no-op, and if the compiler can treat dx as a true compile-time constant (rather than a runtime double), nvcc's constant folding could eliminate that division entirely.\n\nI'm checking whether making the physical parameters (dx, dy, dz, dt*D, etc.) constexpr instead of runtime kernel arguments would let the compiler fold these divisions and multiplications away safely under strict IEEE semantics, since the exact values are preserved. This seems like a safe, semantics-preserving change worth trying — convert the main's const doubles into constexpr globals and drop them as kernel parameters.\n\n","time":{"start":1793107243160,"end":1793107251338},"metadata":{"anthropic":{"signature":""}}}}
{"type":"text","timestamp":1793107251386,"sessionID":"ses_e827fc275ffemXp25tUfLSZTJh","part":{"id":"prt_17d855090001M9FssLb6Kc9XmF","messageID":"msg_17d852b68001G5bWqXfPAq454W","sessionID":"ses_e827fc275ffemXp25tUfLSZTJh","type":"text","text":"Results match the CPU reference on every edge case, including the zero-step path. Performance, however, did not improve with the tiling: the kernel is far below the bandwidth bound. The likely cause is FP64 arithmetic. The RTX 3090 runs FP64 at 1/64 rate, and every cell does three double divisions by `dx*dx`. The physical parameters are compile-time constants in this program (`dx = 1.0`, etc.), so I'll make them `constexpr`. That lets the compiler fold `x / (1.0*1.0)` into `x`, which is exact, so the results stay identical.","time":{"start":1793107251344,"end":1793107251372}}}
